Asobi 1.0 (build 1070) Sep 30, 2026

  • Showcases always open. Make Showcase now gives each showcase a room of its own. A new showcase could pick up the previous room’s key, and its page then said “isn’t available”. Ending a review and reopening it no longer leaves it locked to everyone.
  • Viewers can sign in with their email. Make Showcase asks who can watch: anyone with the link, who signs in with their name and email before it plays (the default), or only the people you name, one link each. The People field takes email addresses.
  • You can see what happens next. After Make Showcase, the Share window shows each step (preparing, uploading, making the email preview) and then what to do: Email…, Copy for Email, Preview and Save GIF….
  • Email you can edit. Email… opens a new Mail message with the recipient and subject filled in. Press ⌘V in it to add the moving preview, linked to the showcase, with the caption and link. The Review Manager’s Links menu says what each item did.
  • Reopened showcases stay showcases, with your Preview link. Reopening a review no longer forgets who opened it, app requests, deliveries or brief receipts.
Earlier updates

1.0 (build 1061) Sep 30, 2026

  • You can always open your own showcase. Every showcase makes a Preview link for you, opened from the Share window and the Review Manager. Your viewing is never counted and never sends a notification.
  • The right link for each person. When a showcase is for named people, the Review Manager’s Links menu lists each person’s own link, with Email…, Copy for Email and Copy Link. It no longer offers the open link, which only says “by invitation”. If someone does open that link, they see the title and the moving preview, with a way to ask for their own link.
  • The email is written for you. A showcase’s Email button opens a new Mail message with a moving preview linked to that person’s own link and a caption with the running time. Copy for Email does the same for Gmail on the web, and Save GIF… saves the preview.
  • The preview starts where you are. It plays 4 seconds from the frame on screen when you choose Make Showcase, and the sheet shows that frame. Portrait pieces get a portrait preview.
  • Link previews in chat. A showcase link pasted into Slack, Messages or LinkedIn shows its title and the moving preview. Review links still show nothing.

1.0 (build 1059) Sep 30, 2026

  • Who watched your showcase. Each showcase now reports how it was watched: who opened it, when, from where and on what; how far they got and whether they finished; the moments people replayed; full screen and sound. The Review Manager shows a watch-through curve, the most-watched moments, and every visit, with Export Viewing CSV…. Asobi tells you when someone opens it and when they finish.
  • Forwarded links ask who is watching. When a person’s link is opened on another device, the new viewer is asked for their name and email before it plays, so a forward becomes a named viewer.

1.0 (build 1058) Sep 30, 2026

  • Showcase links. Review ▸ Make Showcase… makes a link for showing work, not reviewing it: a splash with the title and a play button, a plain player, and a closing card with your contact and a button to your website. Links live on show.byautonomy.com; name the people it is for and each gets their own link. Who watched, and how much, arrives in the next update.

1.0 (build 1053) Sep 30, 2026

  • Watch the speed. The Network window shows the speed as it is measured, with a line of it over the test, green when fast, amber in between, red when slow, and the peak.
  • Thorough Test. Six seconds of eight downloads at once, for a steadier number on a fast line (uses up to 400 MB). Measure Now stays quick.
  • Halation remembers. Switching halation off and on in the Film Lab brings back your settings.
  • A note in the shortcuts. While you type in a text box or note field, letter keys type; press Enter (or the ✓) or Esc to get the shortcuts back.

1.0 (build 1051) Sep 30, 2026

  • A truer connection measurement. Review ▸ Network ▸ Measure Now read far too low on fast lines (11 Mbps on a gigabit connection): it timed one small download including the connection setup. It now warms the connection, times only the data arriving, and fills a fast line with four downloads at once. The number is the speed to the review server, which is what fetching media gets; a speed test to a nearby server can read higher.

1.0 (build 1050) Sep 30, 2026

  • Each tool keeps its colour. Circle in red, switch to Text and type in white, go back to the circle and it is red again. A colour picked with no tool in hand goes to the next tool you pick.
  • T is Text. As in every paint program and on the web page. Trim handles moved to ⇧T.
  • A tick to place text. The text box has a ✓ beside its size buttons; Enter still works.
  • Line opacity that works. It now changes a selected mark, and picking a colour keeps it instead of resetting to solid. Line width, line opacity and fill opacity open as small pop-ups from the palette, and any line width is one pop-up away after the presets. The web toolbar has line opacity too.
  • Who read the brief. The Review Manager shows how many have read the current brief, and who.

1.0 (build 1048) Sep 30, 2026

  • The brief stays with its review. A review brief no longer carries over to other clips or to the next launch; it belongs to the review it was written for. The card only opens over a review.
